newsitem.title: USA: Toy Biz to acquire part of Marvel.
newsitem.headline: Toy Biz to acquire part of Marvel.

text.p: Marvel Entertainment Group Inc said Monday Toy Biz Inc has tentatively agreed to acquire Marvel's publishing and licensing businesses in a reorganization that would provide Marvel's secured lenders cash, equity in a new company and all the stock of Marvel's Fleer/SkyBox and Panini subsidiaries.
It said current Marvel shareholders would receive two series of three-year warrants to buy the new company's stock.
The proposed transaction contemplates acceptance of bids for the newly merged Marvel/Toy Biz, or separate bids for Marvel's publish and licensing business and its Toy Biz stake.

Marvel said the two companies signed a letter of intent calling for Toy Biz to merge with the Marvel character-based businesses and for Marvel's secured lenders to receive cash proceeds of a new $250 million term loan and a 5-year, $170 million note from the merged Marvel/Toy Biz, and 28 percent of the equity of the merged Marvel/Toy Biz in addition to Marvel's other units
Marvel said the first series of warrants its shareholders would receive would entitle them to acquire 7.5 percent of Marvel/Toy Biz's common on a fully diluted basis.
The exercise price would be based upon Marvel/Toy Biz having an enterprise value of $950 million.
The second series would entitle Marvel shareholders to acquire an additional five percent of the common with an exercise price based on Marvel/Toy Biz having an enterprise value of $1.1 billion.
The proposal contemplates the Marvel/Toy Biz transaction would be subject to higher or better offers through an auction process, Marvel said.

Under the auction process, the minimum acceptable bid for Marvel/Toy Biz would yield cash proceeds to Marvel's pre- petition secured lenders of about $430 million and Toy Biz shareholders other than Marvel $285 million, or $14 per share.

As an alternative, Marvel said, a bid may be accepted for the company's publishing and licensing businesses and its about 26.7 percent interest in Toy Biz in an amount at least sufficient to yield cash proceeds to pre-petition secured lenders of about $430 million.
In such instance, Toy Biz's shareholders, other than Marvel would receive a breakup fee of $7 million.
Marvel said its Fleer/SkyBox and Panini businesses will also be marketed and may be sold in a separate auction.
The company said it intends to retain, subject to court approval, an investment banking firm to assist the company in identifying potential bidders and conducting the auctions.
Marvel's lead lender, Chase Manhattan, has indicated its support of this proposed plan, the company said.

Completion of the transactions contemplated by the letter of intent is subject to, among other things, approval by the Marvel and Toy Biz boards, confirmation by the bankruptcy court, and approval of Toy Biz's shareholders.
